items.title: Joe Bushkin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: he has been a guest on Marian McPartland’s “Piano Jazz” series.

ctx.x: Pianist Joe Bushkin was born in New York City on November 7, 1916. He started performing professionally in 1932 with Frank LaMarr at the Roseland Ballroom and since then has played with virtually all the great jazz stars including Louis Armstrong, Eddie Condon and Billie Holiday. Joe is known mostly for his distinctive piano work but also made a mark as a trumpeter and songwriter. His wealth of knowledge about jazz is legendary and he has been a guest on Marian McPartland’s “Piano Jazz” series.
Joe was interviewed in Los Angeles on February 15, 1999, by Monk Rowe, director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We just booked some people for California in July. Sweets Edison, Joe Bushkin, who I had years ago. He’s a very funny guest.

ctx.x: Yeah. Right. I’m glad you said that. Meanwhile we were . . . me in particular, I guess, was anxious to try to be working somewhere. We went to the Embers several times and saw . . . went there . . . saw . . . Joe Bushkin was there. Joe Bushkin was making a great hit at that time. People like Tallulah Bankhead were in the club, swooning at his feet. All that kind of thing. Jimmy knew various people to talk it up, to get me in the club. I forget how it actually happened. Through an agent, I think. A guy named Dave,…
Was that solo? Or was it with a trio? Or what context?
